strings.d1.s0.name: Piazza San Marco
strings.d1.s0.tips: Pigeons and an empty square: come at 07:30 for photos, as crowds swarm after 10:00.
strings.d1.s1.name: Basilica di San Marco
strings.d1.s1.tips: Golden mosaics. Book a timed ticket online (12 EUR); the Pala d'Oro costs extra. Cover shoulders and knees.
strings.d1.s2.name: Palazzo Ducale
strings.d1.s2.tips: The Doge's Palace and the Bridge of Sighs. Book online; the Secret Itineraries tour is optional.
strings.d1.s3.name: Campanile di San Marco
strings.d1.s3.tips: Take the lift up the bell tower for views over the lagoon.
strings.d1.s4.name: Rosticceria Gislon
strings.d1.s4.tips: A stand-up counter behind San Marco: cheap mozzarella in carrozza and arancini.
strings.d1.b0.name: Caffè Florian
strings.d1.b0.tips: The square's café since 1720; the orchestra costs extra.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museo Correr
strings.d1.b1.tips: Included with the Doge's Palace ticket; a museum on the square itself.
strings.d2.s0.name: Rialto Fish Market
strings.d2.s0.tips: A morning market with seafood and vegetables. Closed on Mondays.
strings.d2.s1.name: Rialto Bridge
strings.d2.s1.tips: The bridge over the Grand Canal; quiet in the morning.
strings.d2.s2.name: Cantina Do Mori
strings.d2.s2.tips: A bacaro (Venetian wine bar) since 1462: cicchetti (small bar snacks) and an ombra (small glass of wine), standing.
strings.d2.s3.name: Cannaregio Ghetto
strings.d2.s3.tips: The world's first ghetto, with tall houses and synagogues.
strings.d2.s4.name: Fondamenta della Misericordia
strings.d2.s4.tips: A row of canalside bacari in Cannaregio, including Vino Vero and Al Timon. Come in the evening.
strings.d2.b0.name: Al Timon Cannaregio
strings.d2.b0.tips: Tables on a boat, and cicchetti.
strings.d2.b1.name: Ca' d'Oro
strings.d2.b1.tips: A Gothic palace on the Grand Canal; an alternative to the Ghetto.
strings.d3.s0.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
strings.d3.s0.tips: Venetian painting: Bellini, Titian, Veronese. Book online.
strings.d3.s1.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
strings.d3.s1.tips: Modern art on the canal, with a garden.
strings.d3.s2.name: Punta della Dogana
strings.d3.s2.tips: The tip of the canal, with the Salute church and San Marco across the water.
strings.d3.s3.name: Cantine del Vino già Schiavi
strings.d3.s3.tips: A legendary cicchetti bar. Stand by the canal; it closes at 14:30.
strings.d3.s4.name: Zattere Waterfront
strings.d3.s4.tips: A walk along the Giudecca Canal; try the gianduiotto (chocolate-hazelnut ice cream) at Gelateria Nico.
strings.d3.b0.name: Osteria al Squero
strings.d3.b1.name: Squero di San Trovaso
strings.d3.b1.tips: A gondola-building boatyard; view it from outside.
strings.d4.s0.name: Murano Glass Workshop
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take vaporetto 4.1/4.2 (day pass 25 EUR). Watch a glassblowing demonstration; the Murano Glass Museum costs 10 EUR.
strings.d4.s1.name: Museo del Vetro Murano
strings.d4.s2.name: Burano Colourful Houses
strings.d4.s2.tips: Vaporetto 12, 40 minutes. Brightly painted fishermen's houses and a leaning bell tower.
strings.d4.s3.name: Trattoria al Gatto Nero Burano
strings.d4.s3.tips: Burano's famous risotto di gò (goby fish risotto). Reserve ahead.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mazzorbo Venissa Vineyard
strings.d4.s4.tips: An island linked to Burano by a bridge: a walled vineyard and a quiet stroll. Return by vaporetto.
strings.d4.b0.name: Burano Bussolà Biscuit Shop
strings.d4.b0.tips: Bussolà biscuits; an alternative to Gatto Nero.
strings.d4.b1.name: Torcello Santa Maria Assunta
strings.d4.b1.tips: A cathedral with Byzantine mosaics; an alternative to Mazzorbo.
strings.d5.s0.name: Arsenale di Venezia
strings.d5.s0.tips: The shipyard gate and its lions. Exhibitions in Biennale years (May to November).
strings.d5.s1.name: Via Garibaldi
strings.d5.s1.tips: Castello's local street, with breakfast spots and a market.
strings.d5.s2.name: Giardini della Biennale
strings.d5.s2.tips: The Biennale gardens; a park when there is no exhibition.
strings.d5.s3.name: San Pietro di Castello
strings.d5.s3.tips: Venice's old cathedral, on a quiet island.
strings.d5.s4.name: Trattoria alla Rampa del Piave
strings.d5.s4.tips: A local trattoria on Via Garibaldi, serving seafood pasta.
strings.d5.b0.name: El Refolo Via Garibaldi
strings.d5.b1.name: Scuola di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni
strings.d5.b1.tips: Carpaccio's painting cycle; an alternative to San Pietro.
strings.d6.s0.name: San Giorgio Maggiore
strings.d6.s0.tips: Reach the island by vaporetto 2. A Palladio church, and the bell tower gives the best view of San Marco.
strings.d6.s1.name: Giudecca Walk
strings.d6.s1.tips: A quiet island opposite the Zattere, with the Redentore church.
strings.d6.s2.name: Trattoria Altanella Giudecca
strings.d6.s3.name: Gondola Ride
strings.d6.s3.tips: The official 30-minute fare is 90 EUR (110 at night). Departs from Bacino Orseolo.
strings.d6.s4.name: Vaporetto 1 Grand Canal at Sunset
strings.d6.s4.tips: Line 1 from Piazzale Roma to San Marco. Take a front seat to see the palace facades.
strings.d6.b0.name: Harry's Dolci Giudecca
strings.d6.b0.tips: Cipriani's pastry shop and restaurant on Giudecca; an alternative to Altanella.
strings.d6.b1.name: Fondazione Cini
strings.d6.b1.tips: A monastery tour on San Giorgio; an alternative to Giudecca.
strings.d7.s0.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
strings.d7.s0.tips: Sixty paintings by Tintoretto; use a mirror to see the ceiling.
strings.d7.s1.name: Frari Basilica
strings.d7.s1.tips: Titian's Assumption, in a Gothic church.
strings.d7.s2.name: Pasticceria Tonolo
strings.d7.s2.tips: Venice's best pastry shop: cream pastries and frittelle (carnival fritters).
strings.d7.s3.name: Campo Santa Margherita
strings.d7.s3.tips: The students' square; have a last spritz.
strings.d7.s4.name: Piazzale Roma / Alilaguna Vaporetto
strings.d7.s4.tips: To Marco Polo airport: Alilaguna boat takes 1 hour, the bus 20 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Osteria Bancogiro
strings.d7.b1.name: Ca' Pesaro
strings.d7.b1.tips: A palace of modern art; an alternative to San Rocco.
strings.note0: A single vaporetto ticket costs 9.50 EUR, a 72-hour pass 45 EUR. Venice is walkable (getting lost is normal). From Marco Polo, take the Alilaguna boat or a bus.
strings.note1: Day-visitor fee: 5-10 EUR on selected days from April to July (exempt if you stay in a hotel). San Marco and the Doge's Palace require timed online tickets.
strings.note2: Acqua alta (high water) can occur from November to February, with sirens and temporary walkways. February brings Carnival, January is foggy and uncrowded, and November is quiet.
strings.note3: Cicchetti cost 1.5-3 EUR and an ombra 2 EUR, standing at a bacaro. A sit-down meal is 25-40 EUR, and a café on San Marco 10+ EUR.
strings.note4: Coperto (cover charge) is 3-5 EUR. The official gondola fare is 90 EUR for 30 minutes and can be shared (up to 6 people).
strings.note5: Watch for pickpockets on bridges and in crowds. Suitcase wheels struggle on cobbled streets, so pack light.
